notes.raw:
\*Data above 298 K estimated. 
Phase changes: 720 K, $\alpha-\beta$ transition point of Ca; $\Delta H^{\circ}=0.220$ kcal/mol. 
1112 K, melting point of Ca; $\Delta H^{\circ} = 2.040$ kcal/mol. 
1757 K, boiling point of Ca; $\Delta H^{\circ} = 36.626$ kcal/mol. 
Heat capacity (cal/mol·K) and enthalpy (kcal/mol) equations: 
298.15-2000 K: $Cp^{0} = 11.936 + 1.012 \times 10^{-3} T - 0.799 \times 10^{5} T^{-2}$ 
$H^{\circ}-H_{298}^{\circ}=11.936\times10^{-3}T+0.506\times10^{-6}T^{2}+0.799\times10^{2}T^{-1}-3.872$ 
Reaction equations (kcal/mol): 
298.15-720 K: $\Delta \mathrm{Hr}^{\circ} = -129.788 + 3.933 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} - 2.224 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 106.750 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -129.788 - 3.933 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} + 2.224 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 53.375 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 49.284 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
720-1112 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -131.529 + 7.872 \times 10^{-3} T - 4.596 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} + 45.750 T^{-1}$ 
$\Delta \mathrm{Gr}^{\circ} = -131.529 - 7.872 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} + 4.596 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 22.875 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 75.962 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
1112-1757 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -131.777 + 0.764 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} + 0.346 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 45.750 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta \mathrm{Gr}^{\circ} = -131.777 - 0.764 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} - 0.346 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 22.875 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 31.833 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
1757-2000 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = -171.948 + 2.794 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} + 0.339 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 45.750 \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ 
$\Delta Gr^{\circ} = -171.948 - 2.794 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T} \ln \mathrm{T} - 0.339 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T}^{2} + 22.875 \mathrm{T}^{-1} + 69.851 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{T}$ 
Source: Data from Chase (17) who estimated all above 298 K.
